A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Compute-Optimal Quantization-Aware Training by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite reorganization and added material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, including 757 QAT experiments, scaling-law fits, generalization checks and cooldown-fusion comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains the original training results and adds bootstrap-based analysis of scaling-law parameter significance in Appendix Q.

M1.justification: The optimal-fraction predictor, unified loss scaling law and cooldown-fusion procedure remain unchanged. Equation 4.1 becomes Equation 3.1 with the same fitted formula. Appendix A.4 repairs notation and LSQ attribution without establishing a different quantization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use DCLM and SlimPajama for the same language-modeling tasks. The larger-model checks and quantization scenarios are retained; Appendix Q analyzes existing experimental observations without adding a dataset or task.

E2.justification: Appendix Q adds constrained scaling-law variants, each fixing one parameter to zero, for comparison with unconstrained fits. The existing comparisons against fixed 10% QAT, full-precision training, unfused QAT and separately fitted per-bit laws remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new parameter study introduces controlled refitting with individual parameters fixed to zero or allowed to vary, assessed using loss-fit R2 and optimal-fraction MAE. Existing training configurations, token budgets and evaluation settings are retained; the PDFs do not establish that the original training experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix Q adds systematic ablations of all scaling-law parameters, testing their contributions to both loss prediction and optimal-QAT-fraction prediction. This substantially extends the analysis of the central formula beyond v1's retained dataset, model-size and quantization checks.

E5.justification: v2 introduces 100 bootstrap resamples per parameter, refitting from several initialization seeds, one-sided 95% quantile confidence intervals and significance decisions. v1 has no corresponding parameter-significance analysis; its existing QAT-loss bands describe variation across QAT fractions. The addition concerns refitting existing data, not documented increases in training runs.

E6.justification: Table 10 revises the 425M, 305.8B-token results: fused 2-bit perplexity changes from 12.67 to 12.66 and wasted tokens from -6.1% to -5.9%; 1-bit wasted tokens change from -26.5% to -26.8%. Appendix Q adds significance findings, reporting support under at least one metric for every parameter except alpha, kappa and theta. Most existing results remain identical.

T1.justification: The substantive scaling-law equations and optimal-allocation definitions are retained. Section 4.1 and Appendix O express the already-used wasted-token metric through explicit inverse-loss formulas, while Appendix A.4 fixes derivative notation and indices. These clarify existing mathematics; Appendix Q's hypothesis tests add statistical analysis rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: compute-dependent optimal QAT fractions, a unified predictive scaling law, precision–memory trade-offs and benefits from cooldown fusion. The added takeaway statements summarize these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix E acknowledges overprediction of optimal QAT fractions at low token counts, proposes an undertraining-based explanation and explains the preference for a simpler law. Appendix Q adds a rationale for retaining statistically unsupported constant-shift parameters because of their conceptual meaning.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix O disclose explicit calculations and normalization for wasted-token percentages, improving reproducibility of the existing comparisons. Appendix Q documents the new resampling and refitting procedure. Original architecture, hyperparameter and token-count information is retained after relocation.

R1.justification: Several cited works are replaced, including Mei et al. (2023) with Esser et al. (2020) for LSQ, and Zhang et al. (2021) with Vaswani et al. (2017) for transformers. Adam, mixed-precision and post-training references also change. Positioning relative to prior QAT scaling laws remains stable; the Apertus author update and duplicate Chinchilla removal do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the main narrative: Experimental Setup moves to Appendix A, the scaling-law applications are consolidated into Section 4 with three subsections, and six takeaway summaries structure the presentation. New appendices and expanded explanations accompany this reorganization, although much original prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the left panel's QAT tokens-per-byte axis with QAT fraction and adds a loss colorbar to the right panel. New Figure 9 redisplays existing fitted optima, while Figure 17 adds extensive significance plots. Takeaway boxes, revised Table 2/10 headers and rearranged figure placement substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through parameter-significance analysis, explicit token-savings calculations and discussion of low-token prediction failures. Corrected attributions and clearer figures also help readers assess the work. These are useful refinements, but the experimental coverage, central method and most results remain unchanged; the bootstrap study evaluates parameter necessity without establishing broader predictive validity.
